perspective:
**Alice Lim’s available perspective:**

- I am Alice Lim, a dental hygienist. Austin is my old friend from high school; we are close and talk about our personal and professional lives. I know he works in an office/insurance setting.
- I noticed Austin had become reserved when work came up. I felt concerned and curious, and I suspected he might be hiding something about his job performance. I invited him for coffee.
- I heard Austin say: it was “nothing really,” just usual ups and downs; he wasn’t sure how to handle a few things at work; it was complicated.
- After that, I believed he might be considering a career change because of dissatisfaction at work, and I felt worried. I asked if he’d thought about changing careers and suggested healthcare. I offered to share my experiences and connect him with contacts.
- Austin told me he’d thought about changing but didn’t know what other paths to take; he asked for suggestions, said healthcare sounded interesting, and wanted to know more about my experiences.
- I sensed he was hesitant, which I took as fear of the unknown. I felt frustration and empathy. I told him about my friend Lara, who switched to healthcare in her late 30s and is happier. Austin said that was inspiring but he worried about risks and the initial struggle. I told him that was natural, growth comes from stepping outside comfort zones, and I would support him. He thanked me and said my support and real success stories helped.
- Seeing his openness, I felt encouraged and hopeful. I suggested a career counselor and offered to connect him with friends in healthcare. I said I’d set up a meeting next week. Austin said that would be helpful, appreciated it, and looked forward to it.
- After several discussions and meetings, I believed Austin was ready to take the next steps and appreciated my help; I felt satisfaction and joy. I told him I was proud and asked how he felt. He said he was excited, a bit nervous, and mostly grateful. I proposed regular check-ins; he agreed, saying they’d keep him focused and my perspective helped.
